newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: ESCUDO DIPS BUT NOT SEEN WORRYING BANK OF PORTUGAL.
newsitem.headline: ESCUDO DIPS BUT NOT SEEN WORRYING BANK OF PORTUGAL.

text.p: The escudo slipped against the mark on Tuesday, but the drop was unlikely to worry the Bank of Portugal because the currency was simply following a general European trend, traders said.
The currency was trading at 101.29/31 to the mark at 0911 GMT, a level traders said could provide support. It closed at 101.16/21 on Tuesday.
"The escudo could receive support at 101.30, but everything depends on what happens to other (European) currencies. It is basically accompanying the others, but volume is very thin," said one trader.
Because sales have been light and the escudo was simply moving with other European units, the Bank of Portugal probably would not intervene to boost the escudo, traders said.
Traders said the weaker dollar rather than any fundamental strengthening of the mark was behind the movement on the European crosses.
The dollar has fallen as U.S. bond and stock prices continued to weaken on fears stronger-than-expected U.S. economic growth would spark inflation and force the Federal Reserve to raise rates soon.

It added losses this morning after the Bundesbank said in its August monthly report Germany's inflation has picked up in the last few months and that it would steer its monetary policy toward ensuring inflation remained under control.
